operating_point.platform: CPU (CI's lanes; Actions probe runners, 4 vCPU, for costs and bits)
operating_point.sizes_and_parameters: a 10 um sphere beside a 60 um tube (the done case's scene: sphere_settling_tube's bodies and structures) seen across the tube at 160x120 for the gates, 320x240 and 640x480 for the costs; base step 1 ms; frame periods 1 to 6 steps, sub-frames 1 to 3
operating_point.seeds_and_draws: Hypothesis draws of the period, the sub-frames and the steps taken; the node cached per (period, sub-frames) so a draw runs the compiled step

gate_4_clock.claim: frame_step, age and new_frame are exact over drawn frame periods, sub-frames and base steps: at the step with count n, new_frame is 1 exactly when n is a multiple of the period, frame_step is the last such n (-1 before any step), age is n - frame_step
gate_4_clock.case: tests/sensing/test_in_loop_clock.py: the camera node stepped directly, periods 1 to 6, 1 to 3 sub-frames, up to 40 steps

prediction.why: integer arithmetic on the node's own count

gate_4_clock.metric: exact integer equality of the three outputs at every step

control.plant: the frame condition off by one step ((n + 1) mod P, CAMERA_PLANT=latency)

gate_4_clock.if_wrong: the clock is not the count's: read which output
gate_4_clock.cannot_discriminate_if: the period is 1 (every step is a frame step, so an off-by-one cannot show): the draws include periods above 1 every run

gate_replay.claim: an in-loop frame equals the offline render of its recorded poses with the same key, bit for bit, in the same environment, in both dtypes
gate_replay.case: tests/sensing/test_in_loop_replay.py: the ballistic scene run step by step; the body's pose after each step is the recorded pose; render(...) with mime.sensing.frame_key(seed, frame step)

prediction.unit: largest absolute difference in counts (every array equal)
prediction.why: the same function on the same inputs; XLA may fuse differently inside the compiled step, so a rounding difference is possible and is then reported, not hidden

control.plant: the ring off by one sub-frame (CAMERA_PLANT=ring); a wrong stream key (CAMERA_PLANT=key)
control.resolution: the sphere moves 20 um a step, 1.5 px in the image: a one-step ring error moves the silhouette by more than a count in the band; a key change changes every noisy pixel

gate_replay.if_wrong: inside the compiled step the arithmetic differs from the offline call: report the largest difference and where
gate_replay.cannot_discriminate_if: the body does not move between sub-frames (the ring error is then invisible): the gate's body moves 1.5 px a step

gate_whole_scene.claim: every body appears in the frame unlisted; a hidden body is absent and the build report names it; a body added to the experiment appears
gate_whole_scene.case: tests/sensing/test_in_loop_scene.py: two spheres and a tube; the frame's darkness at each sphere's projected centre

prediction.unit: bodies found at their projected centres, of those unlisted

gate_whole_scene.metric: the frame's counts at the projected centre against the backlight

control.plant: a body dropped from the plan's wiring (CAMERA_PLANT=drop-body)
control.resolution: an opaque sphere of 10 px radius is dark at its centre; the dropped body is full backlight

gate_whole_scene.if_wrong: the roster or the reads missed a body
gate_whole_scene.cannot_discriminate_if: two bodies overlap in the image: the gate places them apart

gate_mounts.claim: a World mount and an apparatus-frame mount each put a body's silhouette centroid where project puts its pose through the mount's transform, within 0.1 px; a moving mount never uses a stale cache
gate_mounts.case: tests/sensing/test_in_loop_mounts.py: the ballistic scene with the camera in the world, and with the camera on a moving frame of the lab fixture's gantry

prediction.basis: measured-before (the camera core's G3: centroid 0.01 px at 15 px radius)
prediction.why: the same projection and coverage as the offline renderer

gate_mounts.metric: centroid of (backlight - frame) against project(camera, pose, body position)

control.plant: the static cache held under a moving mount (CAMERA_PLANT=stale-cache)
control.resolution: the tube's wall edge moves with the camera by more than a pixel between frames

gate_mounts.if_wrong: the mount's transform or the cache is wrong
gate_mounts.cannot_discriminate_if: the frame does not move between the two frames compared: the gate's gantry moves

gate_calibration_import.claim: from_calibration on files OpenCV 4.10 wrote equals the camera built by hand, and project with the imported numbers matches cv2.projectPoints within the camera core's line (64 ulps of the pixel scale)
gate_calibration_import.case: tests/sensing/test_calibration_import.py: YAML and XML files written by cv2.FileStorage once, sha256-pinned, with the points and pixels OpenCV gave

prediction.why: the numbers are read, not computed; project's agreement with OpenCV is the camera core's G1

gate_calibration_import.metric: exact equality of the five coefficients and four matrix numbers; project against cv2's pixels

control.plant: p1 and p2 swapped on import (CAMERA_PLANT=p-swap); k3 dropped (CAMERA_PLANT=k3-drop)
control.resolution: the files carry tangential and k3 terms large enough to move the projected pixels by more than the line

gate_calibration_import.if_wrong: a coefficient order or a file form is misread
gate_calibration_import.cannot_discriminate_if: a file's p1 equals p2 or k3 is zero: the generated files have all five distinct and non-zero

gate_11_refusals.claim: each refusal comes, with its code: frame_period not a whole number of steps (naming the nearest two), rate=, a model beyond five coefficients, a size other than the camera's, recording frames (record= and history=True), a derivative through the camera, a batched study, a body or structure without a closed form, a hide naming nothing, a mount naming no frame

prediction.unit: refusals with the expected code, of each

gate_11_refusals.if_wrong: a refusal is missing or carries another code
gate_11_refusals.cannot_discriminate_if: the experiment is refused earlier for another reason: each case builds without the refused thing and with it

contract_changes.claim: each new path is reached by a test, and a control shows it load-bearing: a camera whose shape setting is ignored fails; a body missing from the roster fails; a mount that is not wired fails; a recordable image is recorded
contract_changes.metric: the shape of the image in the layout against the detector; the reads of the build against the roster
contract_changes.cannot_discriminate_if: the detector is square at class-level shape ()-like sizes: the gate's detector is 160x120

bits.cases: every released program and every merged program with no camera (script A float64 and float32, the sphere in the tube, the energy ledger case), base = camera/core at 400d651, head = this branch's head, one job, one CPU, one thread (bit_compare.py)
bits.prediction: every array np.array_equal: the contract changes add defaults and read nothing when no camera is attached

controls.repeat: the head recorded twice: every array identical
controls.one_ulp: the same program with one parameter one ulp up: arrays differ

costs.how: through the built graph (node_measure.py or built.run), the done case's scene (a sphere and a tube), 320x240 and 640x480, float32 and float64, one thread per XLA CPU device
costs.prediction: a non-frame step adds at most 0.1 ms to the same graph without the camera (the ring shift and the cond's hold); a frame step costs PR 1's disc-window frame (about 1.1 ms at 320x240, 2.5 ms at 640x480 in float32, float64 about 1.4x) plus the response and the noise draw, within 2x; a camera mounted on a moving frame renders the static tube in every frame: about 36 ms at 320x240 and 130 to 200 ms at 640x480 more (PR 1's uncached tube)
costs.measured_at: the camera core's frame times, a different graph; this gate's sizes are measured, not fitted

gate_13_calibration_fit.added: 2026-11-11, after the coordinator's correction put G13 in this PR, and after the clock and replay gates had run; committed before any fit of the sphere grid ran (the replay's own outcome is logged in 'outcomes' as a miss)
gate_13_calibration_fit.claim: Study.fit recovers a camera's intrinsics and distortion (fx, fy, cx, cy, k1, k2) from a 3 x 3 grid of spheres on a tilted plane, rendered live by the in-loop camera with the detector's numbers as leaves; the fitted camera is labelled fitted, with its fit
gate_13_calibration_fit.case: tests/sensing/test_calibration_fit.py: 64x48 detector, spheres of 7 mm radius 20 mm apart, 70 mm from a camera looking 25 degrees off the plane's normal; the target is the same camera's expected counts at the true numbers (noiseless), the declared noise one quantisation step over root twelve (0.29 counts)

prediction.basis: derived (float64): the data are the model's own noiseless counts, so the least-squares optimum is the truth and the recovered error is the optimiser's stop (the default tolerance 1e-9 of the values) times the conditioning of the Gauss-Newton system, which the Fisher information at the start bounds; 100 times the stop is the line. Guess (float32): the line scaled by the ratio of the dtypes' epsilons to the 1/3 power, no measurement behind it
prediction.why: an estimate of a model's parameters from data it generated: it bounds nothing about a real camera; it shows the leaves are the fit's and the derivative through the loop is usable

gate_13_calibration_fit.metric: the recovered numbers against the truth

control.plant: a wrong start (focal 10 % off, the centre 4 px off, k1 0.05 off) is recovered, each of 5 starts (positive control); a frozen leaf (fx left at its wrong declared value, not in start, CAMERA_PLANT=frozen-leaf) is not recovered
control.expected_rate: N/N for the frozen leaf failing the line; 5/5 starts recovered
control.resolution: a frozen fx leaves a focal error of 10 %, 1000 times the line

gate_13_calibration_fit.if_wrong: the fit stalls or stops at a line: read FitResult.ended and why; an insensitive axis in the Fisher information means the grid does not constrain it, and is dropped from the start with that said, not worked around
gate_13_calibration_fit.cannot_discriminate_if: the grid is fronto-parallel (focal length and distance are then degenerate): the plane is tilted, and the Fisher information at the start is read to say which axes it resolves
